summary: Along n_s=15·2^s+1, the Type II divisor certificates are periodic in s for each fixed divisor d (the set of s with d | 4C n_s+1 is a union of classes mod ord_d(2)). Using C≤60, d≤20000 (d≡−1 mod 4C) the union covers all s in [1,2000] except {1,3,6,13,843,1573}; s=3 and s=6 give odd squares 121 and 961, forced uncovered by T1; enlarging d from 3000 to 20000 removes the misses 661, 783, 1948 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z3065.py; out z3065_out.txt, z3065_out_D20000.txt). The misses are sporadic, not a progression, so no periodic (Skolem–Mahler–Lech) obstruction is visible at this range.
not_done: s beyond 2000; the p-adic (Skolem–Mahler–Lech) finiteness argument itself was not written.
next: Push d to 10⁶ for the surviving misses s=1,13,843,1573 and test whether they are covered only by larger d.

summary: Norm compatibility across levels C | C′ fails for an elementary reason: if d | 4C′p+1 and d | 4Cp+1, then d divides (4C′p+1) − (C′/C)(4Cp+1) = 1 − C′/C, so a certificate divisor at level C′ can share a factor with level C only when d | (C′/C − 1), a bounded set. The 'obstruction group' compatibility is therefore trivial at the level of divisors (argument; no table computed).
evidence: argument in summary; FRONTIER.md §2.1 divisor form
